title: Reassignment in a real plan
idea: Use reassignment to model something that changes over time, like a game score or an elevator floor. (Numbers only — text as data comes later.)

exercises.prompt:
A game tracks the current level number. What will this show (three lines)?

level = 1
print(level)
level = 2
print(level)
level = 3
print(level)
exercises.explanation: As the player advances, level is reassigned. Each print shows the level at that point in the plan.

exercises.prompt: Reassignment is a good fit for a number that changes as a game moves forward.
exercises.explanation: Yes! A changing level, score, or floor is exactly what reassignment is for.

exercises.prompt:
An elevator moves up through floors. What will this show (three lines)?

floor = 1
print(floor)
floor = 4
print(floor)
floor = 9
print(floor)
exercises.explanation: Each stop reassigns floor, and each print catches it. A clean way to show progress.

exercises.prompt:
Give the descriptive name for the current player's turn, holding 1.

____ = 1
print(current_turn)
exercises.explanation: A clear name like current_turn tells you exactly what the box is tracking.

exercises.prompt: Arrange a plan that shows a seat count going 0, then 1 (someone sits down).
exercises.explanation: Start at 0, show it, then someone sits (1), show it again. The count changes as the plan runs.

exercises.prompt: Why use a variable called score instead of just printing numbers directly?
options: So we can change the score as the game runs and always print the current one
Because variables are faster to type
There's no reason — it's the same
exercises.explanation: A variable lets the value change over time. We reassign score and reprint it whenever it updates.

exercises.prompt:
What will this show (two lines)?

score = 0
print(score)
score = 10
print(score)
exercises.explanation: The score starts at 0, gets shown, then is reassigned to 10 and shown again. No math — just a new value.

exercises.prompt: Which of these are good uses for reassignment?
options: Tracking a game score that goes up
Showing an elevator moving from floor 1 to floor 9
A countdown timer changing each second
A number that must never, ever change
exercises.explanation: Reassignment shines when a number changes. If a value must never change, you simply don't reassign it.

exercises.prompt: A descriptive name like current_floor makes the plan easier to read than a bare name like f.
exercises.explanation: Yes! Good names make code read like the plan. current_floor says exactly what the box tracks.

exercises.prompt:
A thermostat updates its reading. What shows (three lines)?

temperature = 18
print(temperature)
temperature = 21
print(temperature)
temperature = 24
print(temperature)
exercises.explanation: Each reassignment updates the reading, and each print shows the current temperature. You can model change now!
